display.title: Tanya Shiur 31: Chapter 14, Every Person Can Be a Beinoni (Parshas Bereishis)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur opening the new year's learning: Tanya chapter 14 teaches that every person can be a beinoni at every moment, and links it to the creation story in Parshas Bereishis.
display.summary_long: Shiur 31 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, the first class after the Yomim Tovim, in the week of Shabbos Bereishis. It opens with the power of Tanya's words as a channel of blessing and protection, with a tradition about a Rebbe told that knowing Tanya by heart would protect him on a mission to annul a decree, and with the idea that how one begins the year sets its course, like an arrow on the bow. Chapter 14 follows: the 'midah' of the beinoni is the measure of every person. Unlike an animal, whose traits are fixed by nature (the merciful eagle, the cruel raven), a person has a mind that rules the heart, so anyone can avoid sin in deed, speech and thought, push away a stray thought with words of Torah, and say, 'I do not want to be wicked even for a moment, cut off from Hashem.' The approbations of Rabbi Yehudah Leib HaKohen and Rabbi Zusha of Anipoli are recalled, along with the hidden love every Jew has for Hashem. The class ends with Bereishis: the world of Tohu, where each trait stood alone and shattered, and the world of Tikkun, where traits blend, as a person must blend kindness and strictness.
display.lesson: Every Jew can be a beinoni at every moment: the mind can rule the heart, and saying the Alter Rebbe's words drives away the yetzer hara.
